title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The page belongs to Grothendieck's 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', the continuation of La Longue Marche. The objects are as follows.
- Π̂_{0,3} is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 − {0,1,∞}, a free profinite group on loops l_0, l_1, l_∞ with l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1.
- φ̂ : Π̂_{0,3} → Ŝ^+_{0,3} is a fixed surjection onto a (profinite, 'oriented') quotient group. On the next page it sends l_0 to ε_0, and it involves the elements ρ and σ_∞. This is plausibly the cartographic or symmetry-group quotient.
- M^{!~}_{0,3} is an automorphism-type extension group of Π̂_{0,3}; the '!' means pure, i.e. not permuting the three cusps. M^{!≈}_{0,3} is its subgroup of elements compatible with φ̂.
- M^{!≈}_{0,3}(0) is the subgroup of elements normalising the inertia group L_0 and commuting effectively with φ̂, meaning φ̂∘u = u∘φ̂. In the notes, Cor. 3 characterises this subgroup.

From the previous page. There are two semidirect-product decompositions:
- M^{!≈}_{0,3} = M^{!≈}_{0,3}(0) · Π̂_{0,3}, with M^{!≈}(0) a section of extension (24).
- M^{≈}_{0,3} ≅ M^{!≈}_{0,3}(0) · Ŝ^+_{0,3}, from (36)/(37), obtained by pushing the extension out along the quotient Π̂ → Ŝ^+.

This page. It defines (38)
  Φ : M^{!≈}_{0,3} → M^{≈}_{0,3}
by (39)
  Φ(u·a) = u·φ̂(a), for u ∈ M^{!≈}(0) and a ∈ Π̂_{0,3}.

Why Φ is a homomorphism. Compute (u a)(u' a') = u u' · (u'^{-1}(a)) a'. Then Φ is multiplicative exactly when φ̂(u'^{-1}(a)) = u'^{-1}(φ̂(a)), i.e. when the elements of M^{!≈}(0) commute with φ̂ on the nose and not merely up to inner automorphisms. Grothendieck stresses this point.

Identification with §41. He identifies this Φ with the homomorphism of §41 (p. 316'), restricted to the subgroups M^!_{0,3} = Σ_{0,3} and M_{0,3}. There, Φ could already be defined effectively, not merely up to Π̂_{0,3}- or Ŝ^+_{0,3}-conjugacy.

Goal announced. He proposes to verify effectively that the two Φ's coincide. The next page starts this through the commutation relation (5) for x = l_∞. That relation yields a formula for the 'delicate' parameter β in terms of the 'coarse' parameter γ, which belongs to the GT-type parametrisation (λ, f) of automorphisms satisfying the loop equation.

Role in the larger problem. This is a consistency step: it transports the GT-like automorphism group of π̂_1(P^1 − 3 points) to an action on a quotient (cartographic-type) group compatibly with semidirect-product structures.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The homomorphism claim follows correctly from strict commutation u∘φ̂ = φ̂∘u, and Grothendieck rightly flags that outer commutation would not suffice.

The internal page numbering is inconsistent in the neighbouring transcriptions (previous page labelled 427, next page 422). The previous page's number is probably a misreading of 420 or 421. This is archival, not mathematical.
The verification that the two Φ's agree is only announced on this page, not carried out here.

ideas.what: Homomorphism Φ(u·a) = u·φ̂(a) from the semidirect product M(0)·Π̂ to M(0)·Ŝ^+, valid because M(0) commutes strictly with φ̂
ideas.modern_name: Functoriality of semidirect products / pushout of a group extension along an equivariant quotient map

ideas.what: Distinguishing effective (strict) commutation from commutation up to inner automorphisms (exterior action), and rigidifying via the subgroup normalising the inertia L_0
ideas.modern_name: Lifting outer actions to genuine actions via a tangential base point / normaliser of the inertia subgroup (as in the passage from Out to Aut in GT theory)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld 1990, Ihara; Grothendieck's tangential base points (Longue Marche, Esquisse)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche discuss base points and outer actions in general terms

ideas.what: Program of computing the fine parameter β of GT-type automorphisms from the coarse parameter γ via the commutation relation (announced here, done on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: Parametrisation of GT-hat elements (λ, f) and their action on dessins / cartographic groups

missed.claim: Grothendieck announces an effective verification that two independently defined homomorphisms Φ (§41 and here) coincide, expressed through exact, non-conjugacy-ambiguous formulas. Whether this check is completed later in the manuscript is not visible from this page.
missed.quote: nous nous proposons de voir qu'on devrait pouvoir vérifier l'égalité des homomorphismes Φ du §41 et de ici, de façon effective
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is minor: an internal consistency check of his GT-type formalism. It is of interest only to someone reconstructing his pre-Drinfeld version of GT acting on cartographic quotients.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine bookkeeping step: defining a homomorphism between semidirect products and noting why strict commutation is needed. Its context (a GT-like action on π̂_1 of the thrice-punctured line, compatible with quotients) is historically interesting, but the page itself contains nothing new.
transcription_corrections: Last line: 'des homomorphismes Φ du §41 et del ici' should read roughly 'Φ du §41 et d'ici' (i.e. 'and the one here'), followed by 'de façon effective' with 'effective' underlined.
The insertion '(à restriction près aux sous-groupes M^!_{0,3} = Σ_{0,3} et M_{0,3})' is written above the line after '§41 (p. 316')'; the transcription places it correctly.
'plus particulièrement' is an interlinear insertion replacing a struck 'les' before 'du fait que'; it is underlined in the original.
In (38), the left lower entry is written M^{!≈}_{0,3}(0)·Π̂_{0,3} (with an overwritten M) and the right lower entry is M^{!≈}_{0,3}(0)·Ŝ^+_{0,3}, consistent with (37) on the previous page.
